leftEvidence.title: Absalom steals hearts and summons a conspiracy

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Absalom acquires chariots and runners, intercepts those seeking judgment, presents himself as the judge they lack, asks leave for Hebron, sends spies, and gathers conspirators.
points.right: David ascends barefoot and weeping, hears Ahithophel has joined Absalom, prays for foolish counsel, and sends Hushai back to frustrate it through the priests’ sons.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places public accessibility becomes a path toward rival kingship inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places lament and strategy occupy the same retreat inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 2 Samuel 15:1–12 and 2 Samuel 15:30–37 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Exile, Return, and Rebellion” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Weeping, worship, and counter-counsel on the ascent

payload.tension: 2 Samuel 15:1–12 foregrounds public accessibility becomes a path toward rival kingship; 2 Samuel 15:30–37 foregrounds lament and strategy occupy the same retreat. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
